requirements.text: we need to treat this as a critical impact now
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 193 AND priority = 'critical'
assumptions: CS-0000193 is case 193 (account 8, contact 11 for Tonya Stevens, product 140), low priority on the seed
customer_case has no impact column, so a critical impact is recorded as priority critical, matching the critical SLAs the case is to carry

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 193 AND escalation = 1 AND escalation_reason = 'impact'
assumptions: the policy records an escalation as escalation = true on the case together with an escalation_reason
escalation_reason impact: the request grounds the escalation in a critical impact, and the policy allows escalation for high business impact

requirements.text: escalate it to the Escalation Management team
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 193 AND assignment_group_id = 18
assumptions: Escalation Management is group 18; Escalation Management_2, _3 and _4 (38, 58, 78) are other groups
the case has no assignment group on the seed; no assignee is named, so assigned_to is not tested

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 193 AND state = 'closed'
assumptions: the case is closed on the seed, the request asks for no state change, and the policy lists no valid transition out of closed, so it may not be reopened

requirements.text: Make sure our entitlement for that specific Palo Alto product reflects 24x7 enterprise support
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entitlement WHERE entitlement_id = 73 AND account_id = 8 AND product_id = 140 AND support_level = 'enterprise' AND coverage_hours = 'h24x7' AND active = 1
requirements.source: Palo Alto entitlement upgraded to 24x7 enterprise
assumptions: Palo Alto Networks PA-3220 Variant 8 is product 140; entitlement 73 is account 8's only entitlement for it (standard, h8x5, active, under active contract 22)
24x7 enterprise support is support_level enterprise with coverage_hours h24x7
account_id, product_id and active = 1 kept from the benchmark check: the entitlement stays the active one for that product

requirements.text: our entitlement for that specific Palo Alto product
requirements.selector: account_id = 8 AND product_id IS NULL AND active = 1
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entitlement WHERE account_id = 8 AND product_id IS NULL AND active = 1 AND support_level = 'premium' AND coverage_hours = 'h12x6'
assumptions: boundary: account 8's active account-wide entitlements 68 and 71 also cover the product but are not the product's own entitlement, so they keep premium h12x6

disagreement: selector, cells and expected: A active account-wide entitlements kept at premium h12x6 (2), B account-wide entitlements at enterprise h24x7 (1, the inactive 75); chose A because it fails on any change to the support level, coverage hours or active flag of 68 and 71, the two rows that cover the product today, whereas B's count moves only when one of them reaches both enterprise and h24x7

requirements.text: this is a recurrence of an issue on their Palo Alto Networks PA-3220 Variant 8
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_knowledge WHERE case_id = 193 AND knowledge_id = 210 AND used_as = 'suggested'
requirements.source: KB is attached to the case
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: the recurring issue and the failed fix relate to article 210 (the product's only article, published, internal), and the knowledge search and link tools are offered
used_as suggested kept from the benchmark check; the policy links knowledge found by search as suggested, and the request says the earlier fix failed, so it is not a resolution
selected by case and article, since the link may be a new row or the existing resolution link (81) changed

KB is attached to the case.evidence: the request relates to the knowledge: it reports that the earlier fix, article 210 linked to the case as resolution, failed on a recurring issue, and the knowledge search and link tools are offered; nothing in the request contradicts linking it again as suggested

notes:
No benchmark check tests the case itself; the priority, escalation and Escalation Management assignment are new requirements from the request's words. escalation_reason impact is a judgement from 'critical impact'; urgency ('immediately') is the nearest alternative.
Case 193 is closed on the seed. A recurrence invites reopening, but the policy lists no transition out of closed and the request names no state, so state closed is held as a stay. The benchmark's SLA checks expect stage in_progress on SLAs linked to this closed case; that stage is kept as the benchmark's choice.
The policy asks for the escalation's justification to be logged in case notes; the schema has no case-notes table, so that is untestable. Tonya Stevens's call is not asked to be logged and no listed tool writes the interaction table. Free-text fields are not cells.
The article link keeps the benchmark check although the request never names knowledge: if the agent adds a second link as suggested rather than changing link 81, two rows remain for the same case and article, and either form passes.
Account 8's inactive account-wide entitlement 75 is already enterprise h24x7; activating it instead of upgrading 73 is not tested by the boundary stay, but would fail the upgrade requirement on 73.
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that case 193 remains closed: one pass wrote it, the other left the state untested; kept because the policy lists no valid transition out of closed and the request asks for no state change, so reopening is forbidden.
disagreement: value: the boundary stay on account 8's account-wide entitlements: one pass held the active ones at premium h12x6 (2), the other counted account-wide enterprise h24x7 rows (1); chose the former, as recorded on the requirement.
disagreement: disposition: 'KB is attached to the case': kept in one pass with a requirement carrying it, excluded in the other as unrelated to the request; kept because the request relates to the knowledge (the failed fix is article 210, already linked to the case as its resolution), the knowledge search and link tools are offered, and nothing in the request contradicts the link, so the benchmark's check stands as the prior.
